registered_before: any outcome of this comparison was computed. Already known when it was written: the trades' total P&L (+$12,722 on $1.09M of premium, 95% day-resampled range -$8,654 to +$34,700); entry-skill-20261112-v1 and entry-horizon-20261112-v1 (no direction edge on the stock at 30 minutes or 1 to 5 sessions); hold-limit-20261112-v1 and the other exit studies. From production, only inputs were read for this study: how many fills have a delta, an underlying price and an implied volatility, and the sign of put and call deltas.
question: Did the owner's choice to trade options, instead of an equal-delta stock position opened and closed at the same moments, add or cost money?
why_it_matters: With no direction edge, any profit has to come from the instrument: options gain when the stock moves a lot in either direction and lose to time decay and the spread. If the options beat the stock replay, the owner was paid for the size of moves, which is a different and more promising pattern than direction. If they lost to it, the contracts cost money and a cheaper way to hold the same view is the lesson.

population.trades: every trade in the extract: closed or expired long option trades opened 2025-07-10 to 2026-10-19
population.extract: the file written on 2026-11-11 by `python -m scripts.exit_counterfactual_study extract` (sha256 4ada80b1977230773bd0d919cd3ea42f766b8fcc651d5484fee8253de7c33a47), joined by fill id to one read-only production read of each fill's delta_at_fill and underlying_price_at_fill. The join file's hash is recorded
excluded_and_counted: a fill side other than buy_to_open or sell_to_close, or fills that do not allocate first-in-first-out
an entry fill without a delta or an underlying price
an exit fill without an underlying price
an expired trade whose underlying has no raw daily close on the expiration date
a hold that spans a share split of the underlying (CRWD 2026-07-02, CVNA 2026-05-08, HON 2026-06-29, NFLX 2025-11-17, NOW 2025-12-18)

option_pnl: the trade's own P&L from its actual fills, first in first out (the earlier studies' accounting); an expired remainder is worth 0

stock_replay.entry: each buy_to_open fill opens a stock lot of delta_at_fill x 100 x contracts shares (negative for a put, a short position) at that fill's underlying_price_at_fill
stock_replay.exit: each sell_to_close fill closes, first in first out, the same share of each option lot's contracts and of its stock lot, at that exit fill's underlying_price_at_fill
stock_replay.expiry: shares still open after the last exit close at the underlying's raw daily close on the expiration date
stock_replay.cost: 1 basis point of the traded stock value on each side
stock_replay.shares: fractional shares are allowed; the delta is held fixed for the life of each lot, so the replay holds the exposure the option had at entry
stock_replay.note: a short stock position is not available in the owner's Roth IRA and a delta-equivalent stock position needs far more capital than the option. The replay is a measuring stick, not an alternative the owner could have traded

measure: per trade: instrument difference = option P&L minus stock replay P&L, in dollars
uncertainty: 2,000 bootstrap resamples by New York trading day of first entry (seed 20261113), every scored day in the resampling; 95% two-sided percentile interval on the total instrument difference

periods.independence: neither period is untouched; every result is exploratory

decisions.options added value: the 95% interval of the total difference is above 0 and the total is above 0 in each period
decisions.options cost money: the 95% interval of the total difference is below 0
decisions.what_each_allows: Added value: the size of moves after entry, not their direction, is worth a forward test with recorded bid and ask. Cost money: the contracts lost money against holding the same exposure in stock; a cheaper way to express a view is the lesson, and option choice is the first thing to change in any paper test. No evidence: the instrument neither saved nor sank the results on this history

descriptive_only: total option P&L, total stock replay P&L (direction at the entry delta) and their difference, with the count of trades where each won
the difference by days to expiration at first entry (0-1, 2-7, 8 or more), by side, by period, and same-session versus held past the entry session
the difference per dollar of premium
limits: deltas and underlying prices are the journal's enrichment at the fill minute: delta is a model value backed out of the fill price, and an underlying price is a minute value, not the exact print

the option side is the actual fills, spread included; the stock side assumes 1 basis point a side. A difference therefore includes the option spread, time decay, the change in implied volatility and the gain from large moves, and does not separate them
fixing the delta at entry ignores how a stock position would have been adjusted; the replay is the simplest equal-exposure benchmark
seen data, and dollars are dominated by position size
results: The repository is public. Aggregates and per-trade rows are written outside it and reported to the owner directly; they are not committed.
one_run: one historical run under this id. A changed constant is a new protocol id, recorded beside this one
